records.title: ReMoE: Fully Differentiable Mixture-of-Experts with ReLU Routing
records.reason: ReMoE replaces TopK+Softmax with differentiable ReLU routing and dynamically allocates experts. Its central motivation and experiments focus on differentiability and training scalability; it reports inference throughput within −2.29% to +3.89% of conventional TopK MoE, i.e. roughly comparable speed rather than an inference-efficiency gain. Relevant MoE serving architecture, but evidence does not show inference reduction as its primary objective.

records.title: Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation
records.reason: EPD Disaggregation separates multimodal encoding, LLM prefill and decode onto dedicated resources and adds media-token caching, within-request encoder parallelism, allocation and role switching. Evaluations report up to 15x lower peak memory, up to 22x larger batches, improved SLO attainment, and up to 71% lower TTFT versus non-disaggregated systems. This directly targets multimodal LLM inference serving.

records.title: KVTuner: Sensitivity-Aware Layer-Wise Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient and Nearly Lossless LLM Inference
records.reason: KVTuner selects layer-wise key/value cache precision based on sensitivity and uses offline search configurations online. The paper frames the method as improving LLM inference throughput and latency for long-context/large-batch settings; it reports nearly lossless compression at 3.25 bits for Llama 3.1 8B and 4 bits for Qwen2.5 7B. This directly reduces inference KV-cache memory cost while preserving effectiveness.

records.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?
records.reason: KernelBench measures whether LLMs can generate correct and fast GPU kernels for a broad set of ML workloads. Although efficient kernels may be used by LLM inference systems, the paper's evaluated object is LLM-generated kernel code quality; it does not optimize LLM inference execution or serving. Therefore it is outside this collection's inference-efficiency scope.

records.title: SpargeAttention: Accurate and Training-free Sparse Attention Accelerating Any Model Inference
records.reason: SpargeAttn uses a two-stage online filter to predict attention maps, eliminate selected matrix multiplications, and apply a softmax-aware filter without extra overhead. Its experiments cover diverse language, image and video generation models and report acceleration without degrading end-to-end metrics. The paper directly optimizes inference execution, including LLM attention.

records.title: Progressive Sparse Attention: Algorithm and System Co-design for Efficient Attention in LLM Serving
records.reason: PSA targets long-context LLM serving by adaptively budgeting KV-cache tokens per layer and reducing CPU-GPU interleaving with pipelined execution. The paper reports up to 2.4x lower KV-cache use for attention while maintaining accuracy and up to 1.4x higher serving throughput. This directly optimizes inference memory and serving throughput.

records.title: Block Diffusion: Interpolating Between Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
records.reason: Block Diffusion introduces an LLM generation procedure that caches keys/values between blocks and samples tokens in parallel within a block, addressing inference efficiency and arbitrary-length generation. The paper also provides an optimized block-attention implementation reporting about 15% faster model forward pass than replacing the FlashAttention kernel in its tested A5000 setup. Although the work includes a training method and does not report end-to-end serving throughput, the generation algorithm and measured attention execution are within LLM inference scope.

records.title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
records.reason: MiLo augments low-bit quantized MoE weights with low-rank compensators to recover accuracy and implements Tensor Core-friendly W3A16 GEMM kernels to turn compression into measured inference latency gains. On Mixtral 8×7B with an A100, its backend reports 1.2× speedup at batch size 1 and 1.26× at larger batches against MARLIN. This directly reduces MoE inference memory and latency.

records.title: SeaLLM: Service-Aware and Latency-Optimized Resource Sharing for Large Language Model Inference
records.reason: SeaLLM directly optimizes shared LLM inference services through latency-aware scheduling, placement/replacement and a unified GPU KV cache. Under real-world traces and LLM services, the paper reports up to 13.60x normalized-latency improvement, 18.69x tail-latency improvement and 3.64x SLO-attainment improvement over existing solutions. This is directly within LLM-serving efficiency.

records.title: Efficient and Adaptable Overlapping for Computation and Communication via Signaling and Reordering
records.reason: FlashOverlap hides communication behind GEMM computation through signaling and reordering. The paper explicitly evaluates Llama 3 70B inference with tensor parallelism, including vLLM end-to-end throughput; it identifies GEMM+AllReduce as 31.6%-42.2% of end-to-end duration in tested scenarios. It reports up to 1.65x overlap speedup overall and up to 1.37x lower total GEMM+AllReduce latency on Ascend LLM-shaped cases. Although it also evaluates training and other generative tasks, its direct LLM-inference results make it relevant.

records.title: FreeKV: Boosting KV Cache Retrieval for Efficient LLM Inference
records.reason: FreeKV combines speculative KV retrieval and fine-grained correction with hybrid CPU/GPU layouts and streamed recall to move selection/recall off the critical path while preserving accuracy. Across several scenarios and models, the paper reports near-lossless accuracy and up to 13x speedup over state-of-the-art KV-retrieval methods. This directly improves LLM inference memory access and latency.

records.title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
records.reason: The paper characterizes production LLM-serving KV-cache reuse at a large cloud provider and uses the observed workload patterns to design a workload-aware eviction policy. It reports improved serving performance over workload-agnostic LRU/LFU policies, particularly under limited cache capacity. This directly targets KV-cache management and LLM inference serving.

records.title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
records.reason: This paper directly studies how LLM inference serving systems should be evaluated: it identifies baseline fairness, workload selection, latency/SLO and metric-design pitfalls, then demonstrates the issues through speculative decoding. It contributes an evaluation checklist and empirical analysis rather than an inference-serving mechanism or an efficiency improvement itself. Retained as borderline because its object is LLM inference-system performance and reproducibility, while its contribution is methodological evaluation rather than system optimization.

records.title: Huawei Cloud Model-as-a-Service on the CloudMatrix384 SuperPod
records.reason: This paper describes xDeepServe, Huawei Cloud's production Model-as-a-Service system for large MoE LLMs on CloudMatrix384. It combines decentralized data-parallel serving, expert load balancing, prefill/decode and Transformerless disaggregation, and a memory-semantic communication layer. The paper reports peak decoding of 2,400 tokens/s per Ascend 910C chip at about 50 ms TPOT, and a representative production setup with 900 ms TTFT and 34.8 ms average TPOT. It directly documents LLM inference system design and measurements.

records.title: InternVL3.5: Advancing Open-Source Multimodal Models in Versatility, Reasoning, and Efficiency
records.reason: InternVL3.5 is an MLLM model report, but it presents two explicit inference optimizations: ViR dynamically selects visual-token resolution and DvD separates vision and language computation across GPUs. The paper reports up to 4.05× throughput speedup for the 38B model at 896-pixel resolution with DvD+ViR versus its baseline, while retaining capability evaluations. These are concrete multimodal LLM inference and deployment contributions, so the paper fits the scope.
